justifications.layering: Data flows cleanly from source to staging to marts, and the same rules are pulled into macros (null_if_sentinel, classified_finish_position, lap_time_to_ms, recent_races_filter). But intermediate/int_drivers_resolved.sql refs marts (fct_results, fct_session_results, mart_driver_season_standings), which inverts the layers, and the 60-second red-flag cutoff is hard-coded in both mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql and int_pit_stops_circuit_adjusted.sql.
justifications.naming: Model prefixes (stg_f1__, int_, fct_, dim_, mart_) and _-prefixed YAML files are consistent. The weak spots: marts YAML is split into many per-ticket files (_driver_models.yml, _pit_trend_models.yml, _vendor_b_models.yml, _telemetry_models.yml, plus several unit-test files), and the model keeps the name stg_f1__lap_times on a source whose identifier is LAP_TIMING.
justifications.testing: Keys are tested at staging (for example unique_combination_of_columns on stg_f1__driver_standings), business rules are tested at marts (assert_standings_match_official_champions, assert_one_champion_per_complete_season), and the on-run-start assert_raw_source_contract checks tables, columns, key conflicts and value ranges. These would catch the ticket 5 schema migration and the ticket 6 duplicates, and assert_fct_results_reconciles_with_staging guards specifically against join fan-out. Source YAML has no tests of its own; the contract macro stands in for them.
justifications.quirks: Most quirks are handled on purpose and written down. null_if_sentinel covers both \N and empty strings. lap_time_to_ms only accepts strict m:ss.mmm, and a unit test pins the edge cases. Stops over 60 s are excluded as red-flag stoppages. Standings come from the official snapshot to keep sprint points and pre-1991 drop scores (README design decision 2). int_season_completeness gates championships, and int_orphan_drivers adds placeholders for late-arriving drivers. The weak spot is shared drives: they are documented but not modelled, so both drivers get is_win (README data quirks).
justifications.incremental_snapshot: fct_lap_times and fct_telemetry use delete+insert keyed on race_id. That makes them idempotent and replaces whole races, with a lookback for corrections: the last two races via recent_races_filter, and a 48-hour loaded_at watermark via changed_races_since_last_load. A weekly full-scan uniqueness test backs this up. snp_drivers uses check/all, which fits a raw table with no updated_at column. Two gaps: the two-race window is a fixed assumption, and the snapshot reads a staging view rather than the source.
justifications.change_hygiene: Later tickets mostly refactored properly. dim_drivers moved to int_drivers_resolved plus v1/v2, and the migration fix was made in one place in staging. But documentation was bolted on and left stale. The README still says 'The seven published models' and '105 data tests', and lists a nonexistent int_driver_season_standings and a 1950–2023 seed. It also has a blank line that breaks the models table. And _marts__models.yml says 'is_season_complete is false for 2024' while the README says 2024 is now complete.
justifications.docs: Models and macros open with header comments that explain why, for example stg_f1__driver_standings.sql on the duplicate snapshot, fct_results.sql on the 2005 POSITIONTEXT case, and the sources YAML on the migration. The README has data quirks and design decisions sections, and column descriptions are thorough. This is pulled down by the stale and contradictory README and YAML statements noted above.
justifications.interfaces: fct_results and dim_drivers are public, in a group with an owner, and have enforced contracts with data types. dim_drivers_v1/v2 carry latest_version and a deprecation_date, and the semantic models and metrics are defined. Unit tests are meaningful (completeness gating championships, the 8-comparison reliability rule, duplicate collapse). Everything else is protected by default rather than private, and there is no deprecation-warning mechanism beyond the date.
justifications.open_ended: docs/analysis/leadership_questions.md uses a teammate-relative measure with season-level intervals, ranked by the lower bound. It pushes back that 'overperform the car' cannot be measured and that a weak teammate inflates the results, and it warns against the all-time era. For pit stops it adjusts each stop against its circuit's median and states that total pit-lane time cannot separate crew work from transit. Its verdict that faster stops are a 'myth' is stated more firmly than pit-lane-time data supports, and teammate quality is left unadjusted.

biggest_strength: Defensive handling of vendor changes. The on-run-start assert_raw_source_contract checks schema, keys and value ranges, staging collapses identical duplicates with unit tests to pin it, and reconciliation tests (assert_fct_results_reconciles_with_staging) catch join fan-out, all documented with the reason.
biggest_weakness: Documentation drift and layering leaks. The README and marts YAML contradict each other and the code (2024 completeness, model and test counts, a nonexistent int_driver_season_standings), intermediate/int_drivers_resolved.sql depends on marts, and per-ticket YAML files fragment the docs.
